title: Unit-normalized derived comparison of K-injective mapping-fibre triangles
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with ordinary unbounded derived categories $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume every complex in $\mathcal A$ admits a K-injective resolution, meaning a quasi-isomorphism to a complex receiving only null-homotopic chain maps from acyclic complexes. Let $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], preserving K-injective complexes. Fix its total right derived functor $\mathcal G=RG$ and universal unit $\eta_K:Q_{\mathcal B}(GK)\to\mathcal G(Q_{\mathcal A}K)$, invertible on K-injective $K$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Then there is a unique natural shift isomorphism
$$\sigma_Z:\mathcal G(Z[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathcal G Z)[1]$$
with $\sigma_{QK}\eta_{K[1]}=\eta_K[1]$ for every complex $K$, using the canonical localization and termwise shift identifications. On K-injectives and their shifts it is induced by $G(K[1])\cong(GK)[1]$ under the unit identifications.
Let $P,P'$ be K-injective complexes of $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, let $u:P\to P$ and $u':P'\to P'$ be chain endomorphisms, and let $c:G(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}P'$ be a chain isomorphism with $cG(u)=u'c$. Set $H=\operatorname{Cone}(u)[-1]$ and $H'=\operatorname{Cone}(u')[-1]$, in coordinates $H^r=P^{r-1}\oplus P^r$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-ux,dx)$, and similarly for $H'$. Both $H,H'$ and $G(H)$ are K-injective. There is a natural chain isomorphism $\theta:G(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}H'$ with coordinates $(y,x)\mapsto(cy,cx)$ after the canonical biproduct comparison. Let $r:H\to P$, $b:P\to H[1]$ have coordinates $r(y,x)=x$ and $b(z)=(z,0)$, and similarly $r',b'$. They form the rotated distinguished cone triangles, with
$$cG(r)=r'\theta,\qquad\theta[1]G(b)=b'c$$
after termwise shift identification. Put $\bar c=Q_{\mathcal B}(c)\eta_P^{-1}$ and $\Theta=Q_{\mathcal B}(\theta)\eta_H^{-1}$. With the canonical $Q$-shift identifications understood, these give a morphism of distinguished triangles from $\mathcal G$ of the localized triangle $(H,P,P;r,u,b)$ to the localized triangle $(H',P',P';r',u',b')$, whose connecting square is exactly
$$\Theta[1]\,\sigma_{QH}\,\mathcal G(Qb)=Q(b')\bar c.$$
The comparisons are natural for commuting chain maps of the endomorphism diagrams; no exactness of $G$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 090X, lemma-triangle-K-injective; explicit unit-normalized derived shifted-cone comparison

proof.text: Use composition notation $ab=a\circ b$. Additivity [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] implies $G(0)=0$, $G(-v)=-G(v)$ and preservation of the biproduct identities: the images of the inclusions and projections satisfy $p_i i_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $i_1p_1+i_2p_2=1$. They therefore give the canonical isomorphism $G(A\oplus B)\cong GA\oplus GB$, natural in both variables. Termwise $G$ consequently commutes with shifts, sends $d^2=0$ to $(Gd)^2=0$, and sends a chain homotopy $f-g=dh+hd$ to $Gf-Gg=(Gd)(Gh)+(Gh)(Gd)$. Likewise, for a chain map $f:K\to L$ the biproduct comparison carries $G(C(f))^r=G(L^r\oplus K^{r+1})$ to $GL^r\oplus GK^{r+1}$ and the differential matrix $\begin{pmatrix}d_L&f\\0&-d_K\end{pmatrix}$ to $\begin{pmatrix}Gd_L&Gf\\0&-Gd_K\end{pmatrix}$, i.e. $G(C(f))\cong C(Gf)$ compatibly with $G(i)$, $G(p)$ (cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]). Hence $Q_{\mathcal B}\circ G$ on homotopy categories commutes with shifts and sends cone triangles to cone triangles, so it is the exact functor out of $K(\mathcal A)$ to which [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] applies to give $\mathcal G=RG$ and $\eta$. These observations justify all termwise shift identifications and the induced homotopy-category functor used below.

source.place: Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies: termwise additive functor; elementary biproduct and homotopy identities

proof.text: We verify the cone-closure instance needed here directly from the definition of K-injectivity, rather than presupposing it. For an acyclic complex $N$ and a chain map $f=(a,b):N\to H$, the second component is a chain map $b:N\to P$. Since $P$ is K-injective, take $s^r:N^r\to P^{r-1}$ with $b=ds+sd_N$. The first component of the chain-map equation is $-da-ub=ad_N$. Hence $-d(a+us)=(a+us)d_N$: the residual $a+us$ is a chain map $N\to P[-1]$.

source.place: Tag 090X, lemma-triangle-K-injective; explicit two-component null-homotopy, first component reduction

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift], $P[-1]$ is K-injective. Thus there is $t^r:N^r\to P^{r-2}$ with $a+us=-dt+td_N$. The degree $-1$ map $(t,s):N\to H$ satisfies
$$d_H(t,s)+(t,s)d_N=(-dt-us+td_N,ds+sd_N)=(a,b).$$
This proves $H$ K-injective. Repeating exactly these two component equations with $P',u'$ proves $H'$ K-injective. The hypothesis that $G$ preserves K-injectives now proves $G(H)$ K-injective; no exactness of $G$ was used.

source.place: Tag 090X, lemma-triangle-K-injective; explicit two-component null-homotopy, completion; Tag 070H, definition-K-injective and following shift remark

proof.text:
For a K-injective complex $I$ put $s_I=\eta_I[1]\eta_{I[1]}^{-1}:\mathcal G(Q(I[1]))\to(\mathcal G(QI))[1]$, using [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift] for invertibility of both units. For any chain map $v:I\to J$ between K-injectives, naturality of $\eta$ at $v$ and $v[1]$, together with $G(v[1])=(Gv)[1]$, gives
$$s_J\mathcal G(Q(v[1]))=\mathcal G(Qv)[1]s_I.$$
Indeed replace $\eta_{J[1]}^{-1}\mathcal G(Q(v[1]))$ by $Q(G(v[1]))\eta_{I[1]}^{-1}$, and then use $\eta_JQ(Gv)=\mathcal G(Qv)\eta_I$. Thus $s$ is natural on the K-injective homotopy category.

source.place: Tags 070K/070Y, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies and lemma-K-injective-defined; Tag 05SU, lemma-derived-shift, explicit unit-normalized formula on computing objects

proof.text:
Every derived morphism $a:QI\to QJ$ between K-injective representatives has the form $Qv$ for a chain map modulo homotopy, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Step 1 shows that the computations in step 4 depend only on this homotopy class. Consequently its naturality equality holds for every such $a$, not merely for a chosen chain map; if $a$ is invertible it also holds for its inverse. For each $Z\in D(\mathcal A)$ choose a K-injective $I_Z$ and an isomorphism $e_Z:Z\xrightarrow{\sim}QI_Z$. Such choices exist by the resolution hypothesis and essential surjectivity of the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define
$$\sigma_Z=(\mathcal G(e_Z)[1])^{-1}s_{I_Z}\mathcal G(e_Z[1]).$$

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, Hom bijection; Tag 05SU, lemma-derived-shift: construction on arbitrary derived objects

proof.text:
For a second choice $e'_Z:Z\to QJ_Z$, apply step 5 to $e'_Ze_Z^{-1}$ and cancel its image under $\mathcal G$ to obtain exactly the same $\sigma_Z$. For any $a:Z\to W$, apply that step to $e_Wae_Z^{-1}$; substituting the displayed formula gives
$$\sigma_W\mathcal G(a[1])=\mathcal G(a)[1]\sigma_Z.$$
Every factor defining $\sigma_Z$ is invertible. This proves a natural shift isomorphism on the whole derived category, independent of representatives and resolutions. In particular at $QI$ with $I$ K-injective one may choose $e=1$, so $\sigma_{QI}=s_I$.

source.place: Tag 05SU, lemma-derived-shift: explicit independence and naturality calculations from the preceding Hom bijection

proof.text:
For an arbitrary complex $K$, choose its given quasi-isomorphism $i:K\to I$ to a K-injective. Since $Qi$ is invertible, step 6 gives
$$\sigma_{QK}=(\mathcal G(Qi)[1])^{-1}\eta_I[1]\eta_{I[1]}^{-1}\mathcal G(Q(i[1])).$$
Naturality of $\eta$ first at $i[1]$ and then at $i$ yields
$$\sigma_{QK}\eta_{K[1]}=(\mathcal G(Qi)[1])^{-1}\eta_I[1]Q(Gi)[1]=\eta_K[1].$$
Here only the units at $I,I[1]$ were inverted, as justified in step 4; $Q$ inverts $i$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If another natural shift isomorphism obeys the asserted normalization, evaluating it at K-injective $I$ forces $s_I$ by cancellation of $\eta_{I[1]}$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Naturality at $e_Z$ then forces the formula of step 5 at every $Z$. This proves existence, normalization for every $K$, and uniqueness.

source.place: Tags 05SU and 070Y, lemma-derived-shift and lemma-K-injective-defined; calculation of the unit equation and uniqueness

proof.text: The cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $C(u)^r=P^r\oplus P^{r+1}$, differential $(y,x)\mapsto(dy+ux,-dx)$ and distinguished triangle $QP\xrightarrow{Qu}QP\xrightarrow{Qi}QC(u)\xrightarrow{-Qp}QP[1]$. Its inverse rotation, by (TR2) in [def-weil-triangulated-category], is precisely $QH\xrightarrow{Qr}QP\xrightarrow{Qu}QP\xrightarrow{Qb}QH[1]$: the inverse-rotation first map is $-(-p)[-1]=p[-1]=r$, and $b=i$ after $H[1]=C(u)$. Shifting the differential by $-1$ gives $d_H(y,x)=(-dy-ux,dx)$. The same calculation with primes proves the target triangle distinguished and verifies all signs of $r',u',b'$.

source.place: Cone definition and Tag 014Q, definition-distinguished-triangle; inverse rotation with Tag 0145, definition-triangulated-category

proof.text:
Use the biproduct comparison of step 1 and define $\theta^r=\operatorname{diag}(c^{r-1},c^r)$. It is invertible with inverse $\operatorname{diag}((c^{r-1})^{-1},(c^r)^{-1})$. The chain-map equation is the explicit equality
$$d_{H'}(cy,cx)=(-d'cy-u'cx,d'cx)=(-cG(d)y-cG(u)x,cG(d)x)=\theta G(d_H)(y,x),$$
using that $c$ is a chain map and $cG(u)=u'c$. Projection and inclusion give
$$r'\theta(y,x)=cx=cG(r)(y,x),\qquad \theta[1]G(b)(z)=(cz,0)=b'c(z).$$
Thus all the claimed chain isomorphisms and chain-level squares are established directly, including the connecting square.

source.place: Tag 090X, lemma-triangle-K-injective, cone coordinates; elementary diagonal comparison and projection/inclusion computations

proof.text:
The units at $P,H,H[1]$ are invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], step 3 and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift]. Define $\bar c=Q(c)\eta_P^{-1}$ and $\Theta=Q(\theta)\eta_H^{-1}$. Naturality of $\eta$ at $r$ and $u$, followed by the chain squares of step 9, gives
$$\bar c\mathcal G(Qr)=Q(r')\Theta,\qquad \bar c\mathcal G(Qu)=Q(u')\bar c.$$
For the last arrow write out every factor, using the normalization from step 7 and naturality at $b:P\to H[1]$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\Theta[1]\sigma_{QH}\mathcal G(Qb)
&=Q(\theta)[1]\eta_H^{-1}[1]\sigma_{QH}\mathcal G(Qb)\\
&=Q(\theta)[1]\eta_{H[1]}^{-1}\mathcal G(Qb)\\
&=Q(\theta)[1]Q(Gb)\eta_P^{-1}\\
&=Q(b')Q(c)\eta_P^{-1}=Q(b')\bar c.
\end{aligned}$$
All three components are isomorphisms. Hence these equations give the asserted isomorphism of triangles. Its target is distinguished by step 8, so its source is distinguished by (TR1) [def-weil-triangulated-category].

source.place: Tags 070K/070Y and 05SU; explicit connecting-square computation; Tag 0145, isomorphism invariance of distinguished triangles

proof.text:
To check the final naturality clause, let $v:P\to\widetilde P$ and $v':P'\to\widetilde P'$ be commuting maps of endomorphism diagrams, with $v'c=\widetilde c\,G(v)$. Their induced maps on fibres are $h(y,x)=(vy,vx)$ and $h'(y,x)=(v'y,v'x)$. Computing coordinates gives
$$h'\theta(y,x)=(v'cy,v'cx)=(\widetilde c\,G(v)y,\widetilde c\,G(v)x)=\widetilde\theta\,G(h)(y,x).$$
The same projection and inclusion equations show commutation with $r,u,b$. Naturality of $\eta$ then gives $Q(h')\Theta=\widetilde\Theta\mathcal G(Qh)$ and $Q(v')\bar c=\overline{\widetilde c}\,\mathcal G(Qv)$; naturality of $\sigma$ was proved in step 6. These are exactly the naturality squares of the triangle comparisons.
